list.title: module:js-build-tools
list.description: Import these functions to your own project to customize your build pipeline.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.build
list.description: Runs several processes to build and validate the project. Cleans and lints the source, distributes and minifies, bundles and minifies, creates the readme, then runs the tests.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.bundle
list.description:
Starting at each bundle's own entry point (dist.main for the primary bundle, or its own override from browser.bundles), bundle all the reachable files into a single file per bundle and store them in the specified output directory. A project with no browser.bundles entries gets exactly the one bundle it always did; each additional entry produces its own separate bundle (for example, a render-only variant built from a different entry point than the full bundle).

A bundle's name does double duty: it names the output file (name.js) and, via browserify's standalone option, is also the name its exports are exposed under - as a global when loaded with a bare <script> tag, or as the module when required via CommonJS/AMD. Without this, a bundle built from a real entry point (one that actually exports something) builds successfully but exposes nothing a consumer can reach.

Two escape hatches from browser.config.json keep an unwanted dependency (or a dependency's dependency) out of the bundle: 'ignore' replaces it with an empty object (safe when your code never actually calls into it - for example a library's default option value you always override with your own) and 'exclude' leaves it out entirely (your code must not require it, or provide it another way, such as a separate script tag).

list.title: module:js-build-tools.bundleMinify
list.description: Creates the minified file for every bundle (the primary bundle, plus any additional ones from browser.bundles). The minify step itself never varies per bundle, so this is one shared src()/dest() pipeline (inside minifyFor) fed every bundle's filename at once, rather than one pipeline per bundle - gulp's src() accepts an array of paths natively.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.compileReadme
list.description: Generate the README.md file based off of the template, then append the generated documentation.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.copyFiles
list.description:
Copy files from one place to another - any number of { from, to, base? } entries, configured via copyFiles. A project with no copyFiles entries gets a task that does nothing. Meant to be run explicitly (its own script, e.g. gulp copyFiles), not folded into the default build - a bundle (or any other file this copies) is often the live, publicly-reachable version of something, so publishing it elsewhere should be a deliberate step, not a side effect of every routine local build.

Reuses copyFor (already shared with copyFonts) rather than a fresh src()/dest() pair - that keeps its existing encoding: false fix (Gulp 5's default utf8 handling corrupts binary files such as fonts or a minified bundle) instead of silently losing it in a parallel implementation.

Each entry runs as its own independent copyFor(), awaited via Promise.all rather than merged into one combined stream (mergeStream, the pattern bundle.mjs uses) - that pattern assumes every merged stream ends up at the same shared destination; here, each entry can have a genuinely different one, and merging streams that each already terminate at their own separate dest() hit a real "write after end" error in practice.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.copyFonts
list.description: Move the font files into the browser directory.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.defaultCmd
list.description: Recommended as the default task, runs the simple dist and bundle tasks.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.dist
list.description: Simplified distribution tasks which will use arguments from distFor.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.distMinify
list.description: Creates minified versions of the dist files.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.docs
list.description: Generate the HTML documentation with whichever engine docs.method (or its typescript.enabled-based default) resolves to - see {@link module:partials.resolveDocsMethod}. The standalone counterpart to build's own internal branching, for running gulp docs directly instead of as part of a full build.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.images
list.description: Move and optimize the images into the browser folder using configured settings.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.jsdocDocs
list.description: Generate the HTML documentation of a plain-JavaScript project from its source, with a modern jsdoc theme instead of jsdoc's own classic default. Turn it on with docs.enabled and docs.method: 'jsdoc' (the default when typescript.enabled is off), see {@link module:partials.jsdocDocsFor}.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.sourceLint
list.description: Applies neostandard linting (js-build-tools' chosen style) to the real, hand-written source - not the compiled dist/browser output, which is generated and so was never going to pass a hand-authored-code style check (every compiler/bundler emits its own boilerplate - import aliasing, interop headers - that only looks like a style violation). Includes test files: there is no reason to hold tests to a lower style bar than the rest of the source. When typescript.enabled, the real TypeScript source is linted too, with type-aware rules.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.testFull
list.description: Run all tests with jest. Configure where tests are located by using 'testPath'.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.testQuick
list.description: Run the Jest tests for files which have been modified (based on git status). Configure where tests are located by using 'testPath'.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.typeDocs
list.description: Generate the HTML documentation of a TypeScript project from its source, with the modules mirroring the source folders. Turn it on with docs.enabled, see {@link module:partials.typeDocsFor}.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.typeScript
list.description: Simplified typescript task using tsFor.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.watchFull
list.description: Watch for changes and run the distribution for the changed files, then bundle and test the changed files.

list.title: module:js-build-tools.watchTest
list.description: Watch for changes and run the tests.

list.title: module:partials
list.description: Micro-functions used as components for the main gulp functions.

list.title: module:partials.addToReadme
list.description:
Appends all the jsdoc comments to the readme file. Assumes empty or templated file. Configure this with 'readmeSearch', 'readmePath', 'readmeFile', and 'readmeOptions'.

jsdoc-to-markdown only recognizes .js files, even though it parses real ESM syntax just fine once it reads one - readme.fromEsm (empty by default) names .mjs files to include anyway, converted on the fly (see {@link convertMjsFilesForDocs}) and cleaned up again once this has read them, win or lose.

list.title: module:partials.beginWatcher
list.description: Create a chokidar instance which watches and triggers change when the globed files are modified.

list.title: module:partials.clean
list.description: Deletes all the distribution and browser files (used before create a new build). Configure array of directories to remove with 'cleanPaths'.

list.title: module:partials.copyFor
list.description: Copy some files to a different location.

list.title: module:partials.describeExports
list.description: Describe what a source file exports: whether it has a default export, and whether it has any named exports.

list.title: module:partials.describeFile
list.description: The description of a source file for its module: its first doc comment without the tags (@module, @file, ...), when that comment is a header (it is followed by an import or export, so it does not document a declaration itself), or an empty string.

list.title: module:partials.describeFolder
list.description: The description of a folder for its module: the first doc comment of the folder's index file, without its tags (@module, @file, ...), or an empty string when there is none.

list.title: module:partials.distFor
list.description: Build the distribution for a given source pattern.

list.title: module:partials.distForSrc
list.description: Retrieve the correct distFor search path based on TS Config.

list.title: module:partials.distSeries
list.description: When using TypeScript, ensure that we process the ts first then run babel (dist)

list.title: module:partials.imagesFor
list.description: Move and optimize images into the browser directory.

list.title: module:partials.importModule
list.description: Import an ES module (or any module) with a real dynamic import(), whichever build (ESM or CommonJS) this runs from.

list.title: module:partials.importPeer
list.description: Import an optional peer dependency which ships ESM-only, from the project being built. See {@link requirePeer}.

list.title: module:partials.installHint
list.description: Wrap a stream in a promise that resolves once it finishes writing.

list.title: module:partials.jsdocDocsFor
list.description: Generate the HTML documentation of a plain-JavaScript project with jsdoc, using jsdoc.base.js's own shared config (plugins, includePattern/excludePattern) as the starting point rather than a parallel one - the same base a project's own .jsdoc.conf.js has always been able to extend, just with source.include and the output options generated here instead of hand-maintained per project. Configure this with 'docs.from', 'docs.to', 'docs.index', 'docs.theme' and 'docs.title'.

list.title: module:partials.launchBrowser
list.description: Launch a real headless Chromium browser via Playwright. See {@link loadPlaywright}.

list.title: module:partials.loadImagemin
list.description: Load gulp-imagemin, an optional peer dependency: image optimization is off by default and its binary-download dependency chain is heavy, so it is only required once the images task actually runs, and it is resolved from the consuming project's own directory rather than from this package.

list.title: module:partials.loadPlaywright
list.description: Find Playwright (headless-browser automation) of the project being built, an optional peer dependency only needed by whatever actually drives a real browser - projects which never do never need it installed.

list.title: module:partials.loadTypeDoc
list.description: Find the TypeDoc of the project being built (an optional peer dependency, only needed when the docs task is enabled) and load it, so projects which do not document TypeScript never need it installed.

list.title: module:partials.loadTypescript
list.description: Load the project's own copy of TypeScript (an optional peer dependency, only needed when the typescript task is enabled) from the project being built, so projects which do not use TypeScript never need it installed.

list.title: module:partials.minifyFor
list.description: Minify files and rename the output with '.min' extension.

list.title: module:partials.neostandardLint
list.description:
Lint every file streaming through with neostandard and, unless fix is false, apply the automatic fixes to the file's contents so a following dest() writes the fixed version. Remaining problems are printed along with a summary once the stream ends; they never fail the build.

One ESLint instance is built from the first file's own cwd and reused for the rest of the stream, since every file in a given lint pass shares the same project (and so the same config).

list.title: module:partials.printFileReport
list.description: Print a file's lint messages, if it has any.

list.title: module:partials.readCompilerOptions
list.description: Read a tsconfig.json file into real typescript.CompilerOptions values, using only TypeScript's stable, current, public config-reading API (the same one tsc --project itself uses internally) - never ts.convertCompilerOptionsFromJson, which is exactly the kind of internal/legacy surface that broke gulp-typescript when a removed API call started throwing under TypeScript 7.

list.title: module:partials.readmeTemplate
list.description: Copy a readme template into the README.md file.

list.title: module:partials.removeDirectory
list.description:
Delete a directory and everything in it, resolving only once it is really gone.

A single rm can leave a directory behind - most often when something is still writing into it (a build task, a watcher, a dev server) or has it briefly locked (EBUSY/EPERM/ENOTEMPTY) - which silently leaves stale output for the next build. So: Node's own retry-with-back-off handles the transient errors, then the directory is checked and removed again if it was recreated, and a clear error is raised rather than carrying on with stale output.

list.title: module:partials.requirePeer
list.description: Load an optional peer dependency (one which is only needed once a task runs, so projects which never use that task do not have to install it) with require(), from the project being built rather than from this package. When it is missing the error explains how to install it.

list.title: module:partials.resolveDocsMethod
list.description: Pick which engine generates the HTML documentation: docs.method picks it explicitly; left unset (false, the default), it's inferred from typescript.enabled - every existing TypeScript project's config, which never sets method, keeps producing TypeDoc output exactly as it always has.

list.title: module:partials.resolveJsdocBin
list.description: Resolve jsdoc's own CLI entry point. jsdoc has no stable programmatic Node API for generating HTML docs (unlike TypeDoc's Application.bootstrap()/convert()/generateDocs()) - gulp-jsdoc3, the established gulp wrapper, is stale, and its own README admits jsdoc does not support piped input in the first place, a real anti-pattern for this project's own gulp-stream conventions. Running its real CLI via child_process is the portable way in - confirmed via npm view jsdoc bin, which reports "jsdoc.js" at the package root.

list.title: module:partials.resolveJsdocTheme
list.description: Resolve a jsdoc theme package's own template directory, for jsdoc's own opts.template config key: the folder holding its publish.js. That is the package root for a classic jsdoc template (clean-jsdoc-theme 4.x included), but dist for a bundled one (clean-jsdoc-theme 5.x).

list.title: module:partials.resolvePeerDir
list.description: Resolve the installed directory of an optional peer dependency, from the project being built rather than from this package. Deliberately not requirePeer/importPeer's own require(name + '/package.json') approach - that breaks for any package whose own package.json restricts its exports map and does not expose that subpath (clean-jsdoc-theme does; confirmed live, not assumed - resolving its own package.json throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED in plain Node, and a differently-shaped MODULE_NOT_FOUND under Jest's own resolver, which still is not "not installed" either way). Walking Node's own real module-lookup directories (require.resolve.paths) and checking each on disk sidesteps the exports map entirely - this only ever reads whether <dir>/<name>/package.json exists, never asks the module system to resolve a restricted subpath.

list.title: module:partials.runOnChange
list.description:
Run this function when the watched files are modified.

  1. Find the sub-folders within src path
  2. Maintain the folders, but use distPath for base
  3. Remove base folder and return dist path with correct sub-folders

list.title: module:partials.sassFor
list.description: Build the CSS for a given source pattern.

list.title: module:partials.serveStatic
list.description: Serve a directory's real files over plain HTTP, for anything that needs a page loaded from a real URL rather than a bare file:// path - most commonly, a page using root-relative asset paths (/browser/...), which a file:// load resolves against the filesystem root instead of the page's own directory.

list.title: module:partials.tsFor
list.description: Starting at the source directory, find all the ts files and convert them into the distribution directory.

list.title: module:partials.typeDocsFor
list.description: Generate the HTML documentation of a TypeScript project with TypeDoc, straight from the TypeScript source, so the types (and the comments on them) are documented from where they are defined. The modules mirror the folders of the source, see {@link writeDocEntries}. Configure this with 'docs.from', 'docs.to', 'docs.index', 'docs.title', 'docs.tsconfig' and 'docs.logLevel'.

list.title: module:partials.writeDocEntries
list.description: Write one entry file per folder of the source directory into the entry directory. TypeDoc makes a module of every entry file, so the modules of the documentation mirror the folders. Nested folders are modules of their own, named by their path (utilities/parsers), and a folder's module holds only the files directly in it. The default export of each source file is re-exported under the name of the file (the source files hold one function each), and anything else a file exports is re-exported as it is (that is where the types.ts files go). Index files (the barrels), tests and declaration files are left out, but the first doc comment of a folder's index file becomes the description of its module. A file which sits beside the folders (not an index, main or browser file) is a module of its own, described by its header comment. A source directory with no folders gets a single entry called index.

list.title: module:testHelpers
list.description: Export the setUp helper.

list.title: module:testHelpers.afterEach
list.description: In the Jest.afterEach function call this one to clean up and remove the temp directory.

list.title: module:testHelpers.beforeEach
list.description: In the Jest.beforeEach function call this one to set up the temp directory.

list.title: module:testHelpers.countMatches
list.description: Return number of occurrences of substring in another string.

list.title: module:testHelpers.createTempDir
list.description: Ensure that the del has completed, recursively attempt to delete and recreate

list.title: module:testHelpers.fileExists
list.description: Returns true if the given file or directory exists, otherwise false.

list.title: module:testHelpers.logObject
list.description: Console log objects in a readable format, returns the given object.

list.title: module:testHelpers.removeDirectory
list.description: Delete a directory and subcontents.

list.title: module:testHelpers.setDefaults
list.description: Update the gulp configurations with the test data. Set the test directory where temp files will be created for testing.

list.title: runOnChange~pathRegex
list.description:
1. The original path comes in from src and is a .ts
  2. Discover the outgoing dist path where that file should go
  3. Use the path and dist in tsFor
  4. Take the original path, convert to full file path in dist
  5. Use the dist path found previously in #2
  6. Use the full dist path and the dist outgoing path in distFor
